summary: The candidate captures nearly all central definitions, external inputs, lemmas, and main theorems with generally accurate hypotheses, formulas, pages, and classifications. It is not flawless because two foundational definitions are absent, the Taubes input is only indirectly and less precisely represented, Lemma 2.6 is duplicated and omits the Gold reference's non-torsion qualification, and several entries have typing, terminology, or precision problems.
strengths: Correctly extracts the definition of geometrical simple connectivity and the equivalence between handle decompositions without 1-handles and, for closed manifolds, without 3-handles.
The definition of a class represented by a 2-handle neighborhood is precise and includes the codimension-zero submanifold and induced homology-map formulation.
Accurately covers Theorems 1.4, 1.9, 2.3, and 2.4, as well as Lemma 3.1, with the main numerical and homological hypotheses substantially intact.
Captures the Bauer and Frøyshov external results with attribution, page locators, and most of their technical conditions.
Represents the sphere obstruction corresponding to Theorem 2.8 accurately, despite assigning it a descriptive rather than numbered identifier.
Includes the symplectic Betti-number parity input in an equivalent form, namely that b_2^+ - b_1 is odd.
Page references and numbered theorem or lemma labels generally agree with the Gold reference.
issues: The foundational definition of the Bauer-Furuta stable cohomotopy Seiberg-Witten invariant is missing.
The definition of a symplectic structure and its induced canonical spin^c structure is missing.
The Taubes result is not extracted in its precise standalone form SW_X(s_X)=±1, hence nonzero modulo 2; instead it appears as a derived statement assuming both orientations are symplectic.
Lemma 2.6 is extracted twice as yasui:lemma:2-6 and yasui:lemma:2-handle-sphere, creating avoidable duplication.
Both versions of Lemma 2.6 omit the Gold reference's explicit non-torsion qualification on alpha.

Theorem 1.9 and Theorem 2.4 format the congruence hypotheses ambiguously: b_2^+ is written as not congruent to 1 without an immediately attached mod 4, while mod 4 appears only after the b_2^- condition.
The Chinese term 稳定上同调 is repeatedly used where stable cohomotopy or 稳定上同伦 is intended, weakening mathematical terminology precision.
Entries named Corollary 1.6 and Corollary 1.7 are classified as theorem rather than corollary.
The extra external adjunction-inequality and blow-up-formula entries are too vague to function as properly delimited mathematical claims because they omit their operative hypotheses and conclusions.
No inference hints are provided, so the artifact does not record the dependency structure linking the foundational results to the paper's main theorems.

entryLevelComparison.notes: Precise formulation, at least as strong and explicit as the Gold entry.
No standalone definition of the invariant or its refinement relation to ordinary Seiberg-Witten invariants.
No standalone definition of a symplectic form or canonical spin^c structure.
Records the needed mod-2 consequence only in a specialized two-orientation context, not the precise canonical invariant theorem.
Equivalent parity statement with external attribution.
Core construction and self-intersection conclusion are present, but duplicated and lacking the explicit non-torsion condition.
Faithfully states the nonnegative-self-intersection sphere obstruction.
Main conditions and conclusion are correctly represented.
Substantively correct, but congruence notation is ambiguously delimited.
Correctly states that every second homology class has a 2-handle-neighborhood representation.
Correct main theorem, apart from inconsistent terminology for stable cohomotopy.
Correct intended obstruction, but one mod-4 qualifier is not explicitly attached to b_2^+.
